findings.title: Fireworks October 2026 security incident
findings.summary_md: Fireworks identified a security incident on October 6, 2026 involving unauthorized use of internal Fireworks credentials and access to environment variables used in evaluation jobs in a limited number of customer accounts. An unauthorized third party captured environment variables including API keys and tokens stored as secrets, and Fireworks began containment the same day, directly notified affected customers, revoked identified internal and API keys, and engaged a cybersecurity expert firm. At that stage Fireworks had not detected unauthorized access to customer models, datasets, training data, personal information, or inference traffic within its security perimeter.

findings.title: Update on October 2026 security incident
findings.summary_md: Fireworks updated its October 2026 incident bulletin on November 9, 2026, reporting that a third-party cloud provider hosting Fireworks R&D machines experienced a security incident on October 23 and that on October 24 an unauthorized party used it to reach Fireworks development machines and run an unauthorized workload. The update adds account and billing information, including billing and shipping addresses, invoice and payment history, account balance, and credit usage, plus incomplete model weights and datasets for certain customers, while Fireworks says it does not store payment card numbers. Fireworks links the activity to a financially motivated cybercriminal group pursuing LLMJacking and says the investigation is ongoing.

findings.title: Fireworks Breach: Weights, Billing, LLMjacking (Nov)
findings.summary_md: explainx.ai summarized the November 9, 2026 Fireworks bulletin as adding billing data and some incomplete model weights and datasets to the October breach, tying the case to financially motivated LLMJacking, and describing a second path into development systems through a third-party cloud provider incident on October 23. The post repeats Fireworks guidance to rotate API keys and review third-party credentials identified in customer notices. It frames the case as an AI inference provider breach requiring key rotation.

findings.title: Fireworks Cyberattack Exposes Customer Data And AI Models As Fallout Widens
findings.summary_md: Forbes reported on November 9, 2026 that Fireworks, a popular infrastructure provider helping enterprises and startups build and run AI models, said some customers' datasets and models were accessed by hackers, marking its second known hack in weeks. The article notes two customers told Forbes they had already moved their business off Fireworks systems, with one describing a series of very bad hacks and poor communication. Forbes ties the incident to LLMJacking, where attackers steal access to AI models and resell it without permission.

findings.title: Fireworks AI Expands Breach Disclosure to Datasets and Model Weights
findings.summary_md: Unite.AI reported on November 9, 2026 that Fireworks expanded its October security incident disclosure, with attackers accessing account and billing information and, for a limited group of customers, secrets, datasets, and incomplete model weights. The article states the October 6 incident involved unauthorized use of internal credentials and that Fireworks had not initially detected access to customer models, datasets, training data, personal information, or inference traffic. It adds that billing information covered billing and shipping addresses, invoice and payment history, account balances, and credit usage, while payment card numbers were not stored and were not affected.
